passage: Imrana came to Usha's veranda at dusk with mud on her shoes. "I am sorry," she said. "I promised to help you with the goat pen, but my father needed me at the well, and I could not send word." Usha crossed her arms. She had waited by the pen all afternoon. But Imrana's voice was steady and she looked Usha in the eye as she spoke. "All right. I forgive you. Next time, ask someone to tell me." Usha noticed that she would not lend Imrana her best pencil this week. "But if you forget again, I will tell you straight." Imrana nodded and picked up the bucket.

qa.q: Why could Imrana not help Usha with the goat pen?
qa.a: Her father needed her at the well and she could not send word.

qa.q: What might Usha still be worried about after forgiving Imrana?
qa.a: She may worry it could happen again, so she stays careful for a while, as when she would not lend Imrana her best pencil that week.

qa.q: What worked in how Usha handled the broken promise?
qa.a: She forgave Imrana, told her what to do next time, and said she would speak plainly if Imrana forgot again.

qa.q: How might Imrana have felt when Usha crossed her arms?
qa.a: Imrana probably felt nervous and guilty, and showed it by apologising directly and looking Usha in the eye.

grounding: A child forgives a friend who apologises and explains, stays a little careful, and says she will speak up if it keeps happening.

passage: 'Rukmini, you're not sure whether to forgive Pallavi? Sit here with your Vandana Maasi. When I was ten, my friend Leela told the whole class I was scared of the dark and slept with a lamp on. I wanted to vanish. Two days later she came to my house with her mother's pedas and cried. "They were teasing me and I blurted it out. I'm sorry." I could see she meant it. So I forgave her. I let the anger go, but I didn't tell her any secrets for a long while. When she slipped up again with a small thing the next year, I said straight away, "Leela, that's twice. I need you to stop." She did. We're still friends. Forgiving isn't pretending it didn't hurt, beta.'

How did young Vandana feel after Leela told the class her secret?
qa.a: Humiliated and betrayed; she wanted to vanish.

qa.q: What choice did Vandana make when Leela slipped up again?
qa.a: She said straight away that it was the second time and asked Leela to stop.

qa.q: How might Leela have felt coming to apologise?
qa.a: Ashamed and sorry; she cried and explained she had blurted it out under teasing.

grounding: An aunt recalls forgiving a friend who apologised, staying careful for a while, and speaking up when it happened again.

passage: The science fair started in an hour, and Alka had promised to bring the batteries for their windmill model. She arrived empty-handed and red-eyed. 'I'm so sorry, Nirmala. My little brother had fever all night and I forgot everything.' Nirmala's first feeling was a hot flash of anger. Their model would just sit there. But Alka's hands were shaking. Nirmala took a breath. 'Okay. I'm annoyed, but I believe you. Let's fix it.' They ran to the stationery shop by the gate, counted their coins, and bought two batteries just in time. The blades spun. Later, Nirmala thought it over. She had forgiven Alka. But for the next project, she'd carry the important things herself. And if Alka forgot again, she would say so.

qa.q: What had Alka promised to bring?
qa.a: The batteries for their windmill model.

qa.q: What was Nirmala's first feeling when Alka arrived empty-handed?
qa.a: A hot flash of anger that their model would just sit there.

qa.q: How did Nirmala forgive without pretending nothing happened?
qa.a: She said she was annoyed but believed Alka, fixed the problem with her, and decided to carry important things herself next time.

qa.q: What was it like for Alka arriving without the batteries?
qa.a: Stressful and guilty after a night of her brother's fever; her hands were shaking.

grounding: An hour before a science fair a girl forgives her friend's broken promise, stays careful, and plans to speak up if it recurs.
